This is how I understand it:

If you were to go outside and throw a baseball as hard and fast as you could straight up in the air, the ball would go up pretty high and then gravity would pull it back to Earth.

If you were to take your flashlight outside, point it straight up and turn it on, you would be shooting light particles out of it. But the light travels really fast. It travels at the speed of light which is super, super fast. And light particles are super, super light (as in not heavy). So gravity will try to pull the light back to Earth, but it can't because it's travelling super fast and is not heavy at all. And that light will leave Earth gravitational pull and travel out into space.

The Earth is big, and it has gravity. But when a planet or a star is bigger they will have more gravity. So if you were standing on a bigger planet than Earth, when you threw a ball into the air you would have to throw harder to get it as high. And if you turned on your flashlight, it would be harder for the light to shoot up into space.

Now remember, light particles are really, really small and travel really, really fast. But if you were on a planet or star and you pointed a flashlight up into the sky, and if that planet or star was big enough it would have enough gravity that the light from the flashlight would get pulled back down. So no light would ever leave and go out into space. This is what a black hole is.

You can look up in the sky and see a star shining light from them to you. But if one of these black holes got in between you and that shining star, what would happen is the light from that star would be sucked into the gravitational pull of the black hole and the light wouldn't get to you.
